relevance_note: The paper describes people with germline TNFAIP3 variants and HA20, starting from a novel missense variation, c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro), "identified in three patients from the same family", and summarises the index cases of previously reported TNFAIP3 missense variations.
method_note: Manual extraction; no script was used, every table cell was transcribed by hand and re-checked against the printed Markdown. Table 1 and Table 2 show patients as columns. Table 1 columns carry the paper's own labels (I.1, II.1, II.2). In Table 2 the column header is the variant and each data column is one index case of the report cited in that column, so those people are labelled 'Table 2 column k' (k counting data columns from the left); Table 2 column 1, whose Reference cell says 'Current study', is the proband II.2. The per-patient cell of the Reference row of Table 2 is copied into source_reference_in_review. Scope: rows were given to the three patients of the family, to the healthy mother I.2 (tested and negative for the variant), to the 12 index cases summarised in the literature table (in scope as people from a summary of earlier reports) and to the relatives named in the Family segregation row of Table 2 (father, brother, mother, sister and 'three other family members'), who are described as carrying the variation and being symptomatic; Table 2 column 10 mentions 'sisters' without a number, so no row was created for them. No cell of Table 1 or Table 2 contains the ' / ' stacked-value separator. Table 1 and Table 2 use the word 'No' in a cell; I read it as an explicit negative. Contradictions found: (1) the text says the c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation 'is of uncertain significance' under ACMG criteria whereas Table 2 gives its pathogenic significance as 'Likely pathogenic'; the variant row keeps the Table 2 wording; (2) Table 2 cites 'Chen et al., 2020b' for c.305A>G, p.(Asn102Ser), but reference 4 (the patient report) is Chen et al., 2020a, 2020b being the PremPS tool paper; (3) the Functional consequence cell of the c.1939A>C, p.(Thr647Pro) column cites '(Kadowaki et al., 2021)'. Inheritance: for c.824T>C, p.(Leu275Pro) 'de novo' was not recorded although Table 2 says 'No family history - de novo variation', because the paper never states parental testing. Consanguinity is recorded 'yes' for II.1 as well as II.2 because the paper states that the union of their parents is consanguineous. Normal/negative findings were recorded as the abnormality they rule out.
